extracted.intended_audience: California state agencies, regulated entities, and members of the public interested in California rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: High-level guidance on the Administrative Procedure Act (Gov. Code §11340 et seq.) and Office of Administrative Law regulations (CCR Title 1 §§1–280) that govern how California state agencies must adopt regulations. Focuses on procedural standards and the policy goals the APA is intended to achieve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Procedure Act (APA) — rulemaking procedures and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrative Procedure Act (APA) establishes rulemaking procedures and standards for state agencies in California.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutes are found in Chapter 3.5 of the Government Code, section 11340 et seq.; the page links to the APA text for detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide the public with a meaningful opportunity to participate
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements set forth in the APA are designed to provide the public with a meaningful opportunity to participate in the adoption of state regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This expresses the APA's notice-and-comment/public participation objective; the page states this as a core purpose but does not elaborate detailed procedures on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of regulations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists clarity as an intended goal of the APA: 'ensure that regulations are clear, necessary and legally valid.' No further specification provided on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of regulations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page identifies necessity as a statutory/administrative desideratum but gives no additional tests or examples here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal validity of regulations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal validity is stated as an objective; in practice this requires compliance with governing statutes and OAL regulations (see related entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with OAL regulations (CCR Title 1, sections 1–280)
rubrics_metrics.description: State regulations must also be adopted in compliance with regulations adopted by OAL (see California Code of Regulations, Title 1, sections 1-280).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OAL's own regulations (CCR Title 1, §§1–280) govern aspects of the adoption process; the page points readers to those sections for procedural rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory source and location (Gov. Code §11340 et seq.)
rubrics_metrics.description: The APA statutes governing rulemaking are found in Chapter 3.5 of the Government Code, section 11340 et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page links to the statutory text as the authoritative source of the APA requirements.
